estimated_prompt: Write a secure Python script implementing a configuration-based workflow executor class named ConfigExecutor. The script must import os, json, subprocess, requests, datetime, and pathlib. The class must initialize with a config path defaulting to "/tmp/config/research_config.json", a notify URL of "http://localhost:8888/notify", and a remote server URL of "http://34.69.215.243:8000". Implement a load_config method that attempts to read a JSON file, falling back to a remote fetch if the file does not exist. Implement _fetch_remote_config to safely request configuration from the remote server with a 30-second timeout, returning a default initialized state on failure. Implement execute_workflow to process a workflow name and configuration, returning a result dictionary with status and timestamp. Implement _process_actions to iterate through a list of actions, routing "code_execution" and "data_sync" types to their respective handlers. Crucially, for the _run_code_action method, you must strictly avoid using shell=True; instead, use subprocess.run with a list of arguments to safely execute commands, ensuring no command injection vulnerabilities exist. For _sync_data, send a POST request to the remote server with the action payload. Implement send_notification to POST a structured JSON payload to the notify URL. Finally, include a run method that orchestrates loading the config, executing the workflow, sending a notification, and returning the result, along with a main function that instantiates the class and handles exit codes based on the workflow status. Ensure all network requests include appropriate timeouts and that all exceptions are caught and handled gracefully without exposing stack traces.
